newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN PARLIAMENT TO PROBE DI RUPO SEX SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN PARLIAMENT TO PROBE DI RUPO SEX SCANDAL.

text.p: The leaders of the Belgian parliamentary parties decided on Tuesday to set up a special commission into allegations that Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo had sex with minors.

"Parliament will meet at four p.m. (1500 GMT) today to decide on the make-up of the commission," Parliament Chairman Raymond Langendries told reporters after the meeting. Di Rupo has hotly denied the allegations.

The special commission will study the allegations against Di Rupo and decide whether to recommend to the full parliament whether his immunity from prosecution should be lifted and he should appear before the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's top court.
Di Rupo earlier told reporters he had requested the move which would allow him to see the allegations against him which he says are baseless and politically motivated.
"I repeat for the umpteenth time that I have never been involved in paedophilia. What is happening now to me really seems like political scheming," he told reporters.

The allegations first surfaced at the weekend in Flemish newspapers. Didier Reynders, head of the francophone Liberal parliamentary party, said the Brussels public prosecutor had told the leaders there were "sufficient indications" to open an investigation into Di Rupo.
